metric.why: Distributed AI training is unusually intolerant of network degradation; a lossy fabric shows up as wasted GPU-hours before it shows up as an outage.
metric.metric: Network latency, packet loss, and bandwidth
metric.definition: Continuous measurement of round-trip latency, loss rate, and utilization on the facility's internal fabric and external transit.

reading.body:
Network latency, packet loss, and bandwidth are the operational metrics that catch AI training failures before they become outages. Distributed training is unusually intolerant of network degradation, so a lossy fabric shows up as wasted GPU-hours before it shows up as anything a status page would report.

That distinction matters because it separates this metric from the other two in its category. UPS battery health and generator runtime measure whether power keeps flowing, and SLA uptime compliance measures whether the facility met its contractual promise. Both are binary in practice: the power held or it did not. Fabric latency and loss are continuous, and a facility can sit fully inside its SLA while silently burning compute on retries and stalled collective operations.

The measurement is defined as continuous monitoring of round-trip latency, loss rate, and utilization on both the internal fabric and external transit. That covers the two paths where AI workloads actually degrade, the east-west traffic between accelerators and the north-south links to storage, checkpoints, and data. It is an operations track metric, refreshed on a thirty-day cycle, which is a reasonable cadence for a signal that shifts with congestion and configuration rather than with hardware failure.

What this does not provide is any threshold, baseline, or observed value. There is no number here for acceptable loss, no target latency, and no indication of how any particular facility performs. The data establishes what should be watched and why it matters for training, not what good looks like.
